text:
arya: Heads-up — found a ClusterRoleBinding granting the `deployments-sa` service account cluster-admin in the `infra` namespace. Looks like a leftover from an onboarding script. Noticed it while doing an RBAC audit for GPU pool access.

infra-bot: Alert: ClusterRoleBinding `ci-gpu-probe` created by `ci-bot` at 2024-05-22T14:02Z.

sam: Can you paste the `kubectl get clusterrolebinding ci-gpu-probe -o yaml` output and a couple of relevant audit log lines? Want to see who created it and whether this was used to escalate.

arya: Here’s the CRB snippet I pulled (redacted):
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-gpu-probe
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deployments-sa
  namespace: infra
```
No other subjects. Created by `ci-bot` on 2024-05-22.

kevin: That explains why some deploy pipelines could reach GPU node resources. Also checked KMS logs briefly — we have gaps: KMS decrypt requests are not correlated in our SIEM because the kms-proxy returns 204 for cached envelopes and those events were filtered out by our log-shipper. We need to ensure `cryptokeys.cryptoKeyVersions.decrypt` (GCP) / `kms.decrypt` (AWS) events are captured.

nisha: Immediate mitigation: remove the SA from the ClusterRoleBinding and replace with a namespaced RoleBinding that grants the minimal verbs. For GPU deployers we should only grant `apps/patch` on `statefulsets` and `deployments` in `infra`, and a specific ClusterRole with `get` on `nodes` is dangerous — avoid it. If a node-level action is required, create a tightly-scoped ClusterRole limited to `nodes/proxy` and add auditing.

oliver: Also rotate the `deployments-sa` token and suspend any CI jobs that used it until we verify. Post-incident, run a tenant-wide access review for any `ClusterRoleBinding` created in the last 90 days.

sam: Quick follow-ups: (1) Add a policy gate in CI preventing non-admins from creating `ClusterRoleBinding` objects (fast-fail in PRs). (2) Run `kubeaudit` / `rbac-lookup` on the cluster and fail the build if a CRB grants cluster-admin to a namespaced SA.

infra-bot: Action recorded: ClusterRoleBinding `ci-gpu-probe` modified by `arya` at 2024-05-22T14:10Z — subject `deployments-sa` removed.

arya: I removed the subject and created `infra:gpu-deployer` Role + RoleBinding (namespaced) that grants: `patch, get, list` on `deployments,statefulsets` and `get` on `pods`. I opened a PR to strip `ci-bot` rights in infra/iam repo and filed a vuln ticket: SEC-2024-078.

nisha: I'll open a cloud-security ticket to ensure KMS decrypt events are forwarded to the SIEM and not filtered out (include `responseCode` 204 as a special case). Also want to add `requestBody` capture for kube-apiserver audit policy for the `create`/`bind` verbs so we have full context.

kevin: After we confirm rotation, run an offline replay of the relevant audit slices to detect any past unauthorized GPU allocations. Also smoke-test the workloads on a staging GPU pool with the new role.

sam: I'll add the CI gate and a unit test in infra-iam that rejects CRB changes unless an `approver` label is present.

oliver: Good triage. Once we have rotation and audit adjustments, let's schedule a 30-min postmortem this week to capture root cause and follow-ups.

infra-bot: Ticket created: SEC-2024-078 (RBAC leftover CRB -> privilege propagation). Assigned: nisha.

arya: Marking this thread as resolved for now. Will follow up in the PR and the postmortem notes.
